text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Suleyman Demirel said a military officer was simply "letting off steam" when he criticised the Islamist-led government, and warned against seeing his comments as part of a battle between the ruling coalition and the secularist army.

- The Islamist party of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan is trying to devolve more power to local government under the guise of shrinking the state so that Islamist councils such as Istanbul city council will more easily be able to follow an Islamist agenda.
- All eyes are on parliament as tension rises between the Islamist-led government and secularists.

- President Demirel said any political problems in Turkey should be resolved through democratic elections. His comments came amid persistent criticism of the government and recurrent rumours of a fourth military coup since 1960.

- Islamic foundations and associations have collected five trillion lira ($37 million) worth of sheep skins this year despite an interiour ministry directive ggiving the Turkish Aviation Authority the right to collect the sought-after skins following the Moslem feast of sacrifice.
- Prime Minister Erbakan said political speculation had run wild while he was away on a Moslem Haj pilgrimage in Saudi Arabia, and dismissed speculation the government was on its last legs.
